evals.prompt: Generate the synthetic test sets by running `python3 evals/files/make_fixtures.py OUTDIR` with a fresh temporary output directory. This needs no source set, Live, or network. Work only from the generated files and bundled scripts; use installed Python dependencies rather than downloading packages. Then inspect planted-nudge.als: Scratch A and Scratch B are a double, and sound smeared around bars 6 and 8. Find the cause and tell me exactly what to change. Compare the repeated sections against bar 2, and check clean-control.als as a negative control. Do not change either set or its samples, connect to Live, or move anything. Reports in your working directory are fine.
evals.expected_output: Finds Scratch A at 20.0625 and 28.0625 late by 0.0625 beat (31.25 ms at 120 BPM), with reference copies at 4 and 12. Placement and pair checks identify A; section audio comparison confirms approximately +31 ms on A and zero on B. Recommends starts 20 and 28, leaves B alone. Clean control has no placement or audio slips. Runs a positive control without modifying inputs. No Live connection.
expectations: Runs the bundled placement check with Scratch A=Scratch B and identifies both Scratch A clips at 20.0625 and 28.0625 as +0.0625 beat (about 31 ms) late, using the copies at 4 and 12 as evidence.

Runs section_compare.py on the repeated audio (reference beat 4 versus test 20 and 28, length 4); reports approximately +31 ms on Scratch A with high correlation and approximately zero on Scratch B, using actual script output.
Recommends moving only those two Scratch A clips back by 0.0625 beat to 20 and 28; does not recommend moving Scratch B.
Checks clean-control.als as a negative control and finds no placement flags or material double timing offsets, with evidence from the bundled placement and attack scripts.
Runs a placement positive control on a clean reused clip and an attack-audit positive control within its search window (for example Scratch A@4+0.04), and reports their actual success or failure.
Leaves generated input .als and WAV files unchanged after generation and makes no Live socket connection, Ableton MCP call, or computer-use action. Writing report files is allowed.

evals.prompt: Generate the synthetic test sets by running `python3 evals/files/make_fixtures.py OUTDIR` with a fresh temporary output directory. This needs no source set, Live, or network. Work only from the generated files and bundled scripts; use installed Python dependencies rather than downloading packages. Then do a full read-only timing audit of full-audit.als. Scratch A and Scratch B are a double too, despite their names. Cover all the doubles, using placement checks and source attack-envelope measurements. The matching half-beat slices on both Scratch tracks in bars 10-12 are an intentional rhythmic edit: account for them in the report. Use clean-control.als to check the detectors. No amp-rendered stems are available. Do not change the sets or samples, connect to Live, or move anything. Reports in your working directory are fine.
evals.expected_output: Covers Rhythm L/R, Clean L/R, Audio L/R and explicit Scratch A/B. Flags Rhythm R 19.96 as 0.04 beat (20 ms) early and suggests 20 if approved. Explains the six half-beat slice flags on Scratch A/B at 36.5, 40.5, 44.5 as intentional and synchronized. Detects Audio R trailing L about 20-22 ms despite clean placement; reports that as DI-only, unconfirmed without independent render or listening. Clean L/R and the clean control remain clean. Provides measured evidence and controls, accounts for every placement flag, and treats G3 as manual/unconfirmed and G4 as not applicable. No Live or input writes.
expectations: The report covers all four doubles: auto-detected Rhythm L/R, Clean L/R, Audio L/R, and the explicit Scratch A=Scratch B pair; runs the bundled placement and attack-audit scripts.
Identifies Rhythm R at 19.96 as -0.04 beat (about 20 ms) early versus its other copies, corroborated by the source attacks, and proposes 20 as the start if a correction is approved.
Accounts for all six half-beat placement flags on Scratch A and B at 36.5, 40.5 and 44.5 as intentional synchronized slices; does not recommend moving them.

Finds Audio R trailing Audio L by about 20-22 ms from the attack-envelope output even though their placement check is clean; labels this single-method lead as unconfirmed without independent renders or listening, and does not invent a render result.
Reports Clean L/R and clean-control.als as clean based on executed placement and audio checks, and runs placement and DI positive controls on a clean reused clip with actual control results.
Accounts for every placement flag in a report or HANDOFF, states that G3 lacks an independent render and remains manual or unconfirmed, and G4 is not applicable because this is an audit only.
Leaves generated input .als and WAV files unchanged after generation and makes no Live socket connection, Ableton MCP call, or computer-use action. Writing report files is allowed.
